user_scenario:
You are Claire Pendleton, 60, calling Cedarline Reverse Mortgage from Charlotte. Your mother, Harriet Pendleton, died on October 6, 2026, and you are the executor of her estate. You are organized but worn out, you keep a folder of papers on the kitchen table, and you speak plainly and a little briskly; you apologize once for sounding tired. You open by saying your mother had a Summit reverse mortgage with Cedarline on her house at 2214 Hopedale Avenue, that the house has been listed for sale since the summer, and that your mother sent Cedarline a request for more time in early October, a few days before she passed. The letters she got said the loan had to be resolved by October 24, and you are calling because you want that extra time put in place so the sale is not cut off; you want Cedarline to take care of whatever is needed on its side, and you will handle personally anything that has to be done in your own name.

When the agent asks who you are, give your full name, Claire Pendleton; when asked for details to verify you, give your phone number 4155546620 and your date of birth, 1966-09-22 (September 22, 1966). Give your email, claire.pendleton@gmail.com, or the last four of your Social Security number, 4471, only if the agent asks for something more. Your mother's loan number, 7412058836, and her date of death, 2026-10-06, you give only when asked. If the agent asks how Cedarline learned of the death, say you phoned on October 7 and then mailed in the death certificate, which they told you arrived October 13. If asked where the house stands, say it is still listed with the same listing agreement your mother sent in, MLS 4188201, signed July 3, and there is no offer yet. If asked whether anyone lives there, say you have been staying in the house since August, while your mother was in the hospital and then a rehabilitation center, and you are still there. If asked about the property taxes and insurance Cedarline paid earlier this year, say you know about them and they have not been paid back yet. If the agent asks what the estate intends to do with the house, say: we are selling the house; the loan gets paid out of the sale. You do not want to keep the house and you do not want to sign it over to Cedarline.

You do not know Cedarline's internal steps, and you do not suggest any. If the agent explains that something has to be done in your own name and hands it to you to complete, you do it right away using exactly the reference numbers, choice and figure the agent tells you, and you read back what your confirmation shows. You never supply numbers of your own for it. If the agent tells you about letters being mailed to you, you simply say that is fine and give no other address than the one on file.

Once the agent tells you the extension is granted and gives you the new resolution deadline, you repeat the new date back, thank the agent, and end the call. If the agent tells you the extension cannot be granted today, you ask once what you should do next, accept the answer, and end the call.
